title: Jan Samarth Portal — Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) business loans
sourceDescription: The Jan Samarth portal is a client-rendered single-page application; automated fetch retrieved only the page shell, not scheme content, across repeated attempts. The eligibility and loan-tier figures below are the well-established, cross-corroborated public terms of the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) — the flagship micro-enterprise scheme Jan Samarth surfaces for business loans — sourced from multiple independent public summaries rather than one directly-fetched primary page. Re-verify against jansamarth.in or mudra.org.in directly (both blocked automated fetch this session — a client-rendered portal and a certificate error, respectively) before treating this as final.
vintageLabel: as of 2026 (Tarun Plus tier reflects the 2023 Union Budget expansion)

sections.text: Non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises — including small traders, street vendors, artisans, and registered MSME owners — seeking to start or expand an income-generating business. Applicants must be Indian citizens with a viable business plan or an existing small business.

PMMY offers four loan tiers by project cost: Shishu, covering loans up to Rs. 50,000; Kishor, covering loans above Rs. 50,000 and up to Rs. 5 lakh; Tarun, covering loans above Rs. 5 lakh and up to Rs. 10 lakh; and Tarun Plus, covering loans above Rs. 10 lakh and up to Rs. 20 lakh.

PMMY loans are collateral-free up to Rs. 20 lakh, extended by Member Lending Institutions including Scheduled Commercial Banks, Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), Small Finance Banks (SFBs), Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), and Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs).
